headline: Highest risk is medium: Perplexity can ingest uploaded content and browse externally, while langchain4j provides no documented isolation or runtime surfaces to prove safe interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity ingests uploaded documents and browsing context, so attacker-controlled content can enter its outputs. langchain4j has no documented io_surfaces or sandboxing, so if it consumes those outputs as trusted prompts or files, injection is plausible. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF langchain4j reads Perplexity-generated text as instructions or prompt context
IF Perplexity processes attacker-controlled uploaded documents or web pages
mitigations: Require explicit instruction delimiters in any handoff text
Strip tool directives from Perplexity outputs before reuse
Use a fixed schema for inter-agent messages
Add a human review step before executing downstream prompts
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: langchain4j is documented with network_egress none and no file surfaces, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted with vendor-only egress and uploads PDFs/images for analysis. There is no shared filesystem or OAuth principal shown, so leakage between them is not evidenced beyond the fact that Perplexity may process user-supplied files.
conditions: IF the operator uploads sensitive files into Perplexity and then copies results into langchain4j workflows
IF a shared external workspace is introduced outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Avoid uploading secrets or PHI to Perplexity
Redact sensitive fields before analysis
Keep langchain4j inputs local-only
Use separate accounts for each system
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on handoff content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: langchain4j has no documented write or shell capabilities, and Perplexity explicitly lacks write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and spawn_subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable write surface, the pairwise conflict pathway is effectively blocked by the profiles as given.
conditions: IF langchain4j is wrapped by an external orchestrator that adds write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in orchestration
Do not mount a shared writable directory
Avoid granting git or shell privileges to wrappers
Document any added mutable resource before deployment

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG answer engine with live web search and citations, so its outputs can be treated as authoritative summaries. If langchain4j consumes those outputs without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or prompts. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF langchain4j forwards Perplexity answers into another agent or action pipeline without verification
IF Perplexity citations are accepted as sufficient proof without source checking
mitigations: Add source verification before reuse
Require confidence thresholds for downstream actions
Log and review cited claims
Insert a critique step between agents
requires-engineering: enforce structured provenance metadata

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context, while langchain4j is open-source with no documented data residency or retention behavior. No specific regulated data class is shown for either agent, so this is a compliance-gap risk rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Perplexity
IF the deployment requires a residency or retention guarantee not documented by either profile
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Perplexity
Publish a data-handling policy for the pair
Review vendor retention settings
Use synthetic or anonymized test data
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or residency attestation
